**6B.9 Research Note**
Overall: mostly no. I found a few genuine institution-building signals, but they are narrow, technical, and often partner-supported. The core political and accountability institutions still looked personalized, captured, and fragile by 2024.

**Positive evidence**
- **Bangladesh Public Procurement Authority: e-GP reform** | Bangladesh Public Procurement Authority | March 6, 2024 | [source](https://bppa.gov.bd/media-communication/news-1446.html) | BPPA said e-GP was mandatory for government agencies, with broad registration and improved transparency, efficiency, and competition. This is one of the clearest signs of a durable administrative institution, not just a leader-centric program. | `6B.9` `6B.5`
- **Advancing healthcare excellence: national medical education strategy** | WHO Bangladesh | March 4, 2024 | [source](https://www.who.int/bangladesh/news/detail/04-03-2024-advancing-healthcare-excellence-who-s-role-in-developing-the-first-national-medical-education-strategy-in-bangladesh) | The health ministry, with WHO support, launched Bangladesh’s first national medical education strategy using health-workforce studies and a technical working group. That points to an evidence-based institution that could survive beyond Hasina personally, but the evidence is sector-specific. | `6B.9` `6B.5` `6B.8`
- **Second JEE using eJEE platform** | WHO | July 11, 2024 | [source](https://www.who.int/southeastasia/news/detail/11-07-2024-2nd-jee-bn) | Bangladesh completed a peer-reviewed Joint External Evaluation using a formal platform, with identified strengths, gaps, and priority actions. This is a real institutional capacity signal because it embeds measurement and correction into the health-security bureaucracy. | `6B.9` `6B.5`
- **Bangladesh receives $900 million for resilience and reforms** | World Bank | June 21, 2024 | [source](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/06/21/bangladesh-receives-900-million-world-bank-financing-to-increase-economic-and-urban-resilience-for-sustainable-growth) | The World Bank backed fiscal and financial-sector reforms, tax changes, procurement reform, and climate-resilient urban management. This supports a partial institution-building reading, but it is reform design rather than proof of durable institutional success. | `6B.9` `6B.5` `6B.6`
- **Bangladesh receives $900 million to improve environment sustainability, urban and climate resilience** | World Bank | December 22, 2024 | [source](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/12/23/bangladesh-receives-900-million-world-bank-financing-to-improve-environment-sustainability-urban-and-climate-resilience) | Late-2024 financing targeted climate-resilient urban infrastructure, roads, bus terminals, markets, parks, toilets, and bridges. That suggests some long-horizon public-capacity building, though it is still not strong proof of institutions that outlast personal rule. | `6B.9` `6B.6`

**Negative evidence**
- **Freedom in the World 2024: Bangladesh** | Freedom House | 2024 | [source](https://freedomhouse.org/country/bangladesh/freedom-world/2024) | Freedom House described harassment of the opposition and media, politicized anticorruption enforcement, questioned Election Commission independence, and discriminatory treatment of minorities and refugees. That is strong evidence against durable, neutral institutions. | `6B.9` `6B.7` `6B.8`
- **Freedom in the Net 2024: Bangladesh** | Freedom House | 2024 | [source](https://freedomhouse.org/country/bangladesh/freedom-net/2024) | The report says the Awami League manipulated the online information environment, blocked major news sites, and throttled communications around BNP rallies, with later shutdowns during unrest. This is evidence of control over information institutions rather than building ones that can survive a leader’s exit. | `6B.9` `1B.8` `6B.8`
- **Bangladesh repression, security-force abuses discredit elections** | Human Rights Watch | January 11, 2024 | [source](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/01/11/bangladesh-repression-security-force-abuses-discredit-elections) | HRW reported arrests for criticism and widespread repression before the election. A system that chills dissent early in the year is not building independent civic institutions that can outlast the ruler. | `6B.9` `1B.8` `6B.8`
- **Bangladesh’s election extending Hasina’s rule were not credible** | Associated Press | January 8, 2024 | [source](https://ny1.com/nyc/all-boroughs/ap-top-news/2024/01/09/the-us-and-uk-say-bangladeshs-elections-extending-hasinas-rule-were-not-credible) | AP reported the vote was boycotted by the opposition and viewed as not credible by key foreign partners. That undercuts any claim that Hasina was leaving behind a durable, legitimate electoral institution. | `6B.9` `1B.5` `1B.8`
- **Bangladesh PM Hasina blames opposition, curfew to remain** | Reuters | July 22, 2024 | [source](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/bangladesh-pm-hasina-blames-opposition-for-violence-curfew-to-remain-3528153) | Hasina kept the curfew in place and blamed political opponents for the violence rather than pivoting to institutional accountability or de-escalation. That looks like personalized regime defense, not durable institution-building. | `6B.9` `6B.5` `6B.8`
- **Bangladesh crackdown leaves more than 170 dead** | UN OHCHR | July 26, 2024 | [source](https://bangladesh.un.org/en/275065-bangladesh-t%C3%BCrk-decries-government-crackdown-urges-respect-international-human-rights) | The UN said more than 170 people were killed, internet shutdowns increased impunity, and injured people were denied medical care. A state that solves crises through opacity and coercion is not building resilient institutions. | `6B.9` `6B.6` `6B.8`
- **Bangladesh was left with a lawless economy** | The Daily Star | October 31, 2024 | [source](https://www.thedailystar.net/news/bangladesh/news/al-govt-created-lawless-economy-3741796) | A white-paper lead said authoritarian practices produced crony capitalism and a nexus of bureaucrats, political leaders, and business interests that captured public organizations. That is direct evidence against institution-building beyond personal rule. | `6B.9` `6B.7`
- **Rooppur as a white elephant** | TBS News | October 5, 2024 | [source](https://www.tbsnews.net/bangladesh/energy/rooppur-power-plant-was-al-govts-white-elephant-energy-sector-experts-958801) | Energy-sector experts described Rooppur as mismanaged and corruption-linked under the Awami League government. This is indirect, but it reinforces the picture of weak institutional discipline and patronage. | `6B.9` `6B.7`

**Synthesis**
- The best positive evidence is real but narrow: procurement reform, health-workforce planning, technical evaluations, and climate-resilience spending.
- The strongest negative evidence is broader and more structural: politicized elections, captured oversight institutions, censorship, and coercive crisis management.
- Net: Hasina did not clearly build durable social institutions that were independent of her personal rule; she did leave some technocratic and administrative reforms, but they were not enough to offset the personalization and capture in the core political system.

**Search gap**
- I did not find strong evidence of deliberately insulated, leader-independent institutions in elections, courts, media, or anticorruption that would survive a change in ruler.
- The most credible positives were sectoral and often externally supported, so they do not show a broad, durable institutional settlement.
